content.summary: Welcome to Unit B2.2-M04. In this reading mission, you will explore how investigative journalism uses causative verbs and passive reporting structures to report complex stories safely and professionally. You will learn how to describe services arranged for others and how news articles present claims without naming direct sources.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Causative structures (have/get something done) and impersonal passive reporting verbs (it is alleged, he is reported to have).
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Key terms for investigations, property renovations, inspections, and formal allegations.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning news articles for specific causative structures and identifying passive attribution of claims.

learningObjectives: Understand complex news texts and investigative reports about professional services and media claims.
Locate specific causative examples and passive reporting structures within a reading passage.
Recognize and apply grammar patterns involving have/get something done and impersonal passives.

contextWarmup.prompt: When a company needs to check its financial records, what do they usually do?
options: They have an independent auditor inspect the accounts.
They inspect the accounts themselves without any training.
They ignore the records and hope for the best outcome.
contextWarmup.explanation: Organizations routinely hire external professionals to examine their records objectively, which is a classic example of having something done.

rules: HAVE something DONE: Subject + have + object + past participle. Used to state that the subject arranges for someone else to do a task.
GET something DONE: Subject + get + object + past participle. Similar to have, but more informal and often implies personal effort or slight difficulty.
IMPERSONAL PASSIVE with IT: It + is/was + past participle + that-clause. Used to report claims or opinions without naming a direct source.
IMPERSONAL PASSIVE with SUBJECT: Subject + is/was + past participle + to-infinitive. A formal structure frequently found in news reports.
REPORTING VERBS: Common verbs include say, believe, think, allege, report, claim, consider, know, expect, and understand.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often mix up active voice with causative structures, saying 'I had my car service' instead of 'I had my car serviced'.
commonTrap.wrong: She had her kitchen renovate by a professional contractor.
commonTrap.correct: She had her kitchen renovated by a professional contractor.

paragraphs: Last month, local residents noticed unusual activity at the old heritage building downtown. The mayor is reported to have known about the financial irregularities earlier this year, although official statements deny any involvement. subModules.title: Writing Mission: Causative Verbs & Passive Reporting Structures

content.summary: Master formal reporting and causative structures to elevate your professional and journalistic writing at the B2 level.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Have/Get Something Done (Causative)
blueprintItems.example: She had her laptop repaired by a technician yesterday.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Impersonal Passive with 'It'
blueprintItems.formula: It + passive reporting verb (is/was alleged, believed, reported) + that-clause
blueprintItems.example: It is alleged that the director misused corporate funds.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Impersonal Passive with Subject + Infinitive
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + passive reporting verb + to-infinitive (present or perfect)
blueprintItems.example: The CEO is reported to have signed the agreement.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place the object between the causative verb and the past participle.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I had repaired my car yesterday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I had my car repaired yesterday.
mechanicsRules.why: In causative structures, the object receiving the action must immediately follow 'have' or 'get'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the perfect infinitive (to have done) when the action in the infinitive clause happened prior to the reporting time.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He is rumored to steal the documents last year.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He is rumored to have stolen the documents last year.
mechanicsRules.why: A past event referenced in an impersonal passive structure requires the 'to have + V3' construction.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not include an active agent in impersonal passive structures unless preceded by 'by', though omission is preferred.
mechanicsRules.badExample: It is believed by people that inflation will rise.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: It is believed that inflation will rise.
mechanicsRules.why: Impersonal reporting structures are designed to sound objective by omitting general agents.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Causative Verbs & Passive Reporting Structures

content.summary: Mastering advanced spoken English at the B2 level requires precise control over sentence stress, weak forms in auxiliary verbs, and the smooth linking of multi-syllable academic vocabulary. When delivering formal statements using passive reporting structures and causative verbs, clear articulation prevents ambiguity and projects professional authority.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on pausing slightly after reporting clauses such as it is alleged or it is reported. Ensure that auxiliary verbs like have and get are unstressed in casual causative constructions unless you need to contrast them.

pillars.name: Causative Stress
pillars.target: Emphasizing the object and the past participle
pillars.explanation: In sentences using have or get something done, the primary sentence stress falls on the main object and the final past participle verb, leaving the causative verb weak.

pillars.name: Reporting Intonation
pillars.target: Falling tone on authoritative reporting clauses
pillars.explanation: When introducing claims with passive reporting verbs, use a falling intonation on the introductory clause to signal objective reporting or formal journalism.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity in Academic Lexicon
pillars.target: Precise articulation of low and mid vowels
pillars.explanation: Words such as allege, undergo, and commissioned require crisp vowel sounds to ensure listener comprehension in formal academic or professional discussions.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The primary stress shifts from the second syllable in the verb to the third syllable in the noun form.
The stress moves to the final syllable in the past tense form.

The stress remains on the second syllable when adding the nominal suffix.

reading.question: What activity did local residents notice downtown last month?

A major street festival outside city hall

writing.instruction: Transform the active sentence into a causative sentence using 'have': 'A mechanic repaired my car yesterday.'
writing.promptText: Rewrite using 'have': A mechanic repaired my car yesterday.
targetAnswers: I had my car repaired yesterday.
She had her car repaired yesterday.
writing.explanation: To use the causative structure, place the object 'my car' between 'had' and the past participle 'repaired'.

writing.instruction: Transform the sentence using 'get': 'They will clean our carpets tomorrow.'
writing.promptText: Rewrite using 'get': They will clean our carpets tomorrow.
writing.hint: Subject + will get + object + past participle.
targetAnswers: We will get our carpets cleaned tomorrow.
They will get their carpets cleaned tomorrow.
writing.explanation: The causative structure with 'get' follows the exact same word order: subject + get + object + V3.

writing.instruction: Change the active reporting sentence into an impersonal passive sentence starting with 'It': 'People believe that the economy will recover soon.'
targetAnswers: It is believed that the economy will recover soon.
writing.explanation: Impersonal passive structure uses 'It' followed by the passive reporting verb and the unchanged that-clause.

writing.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using the subject + infinitive structure: 'People report that the stolen artwork was found in a warehouse.'
writing.promptText: Rewrite starting with 'The stolen artwork is reported...':
writing.hint: Use the perfect infinitive (to have been found) because the action happened in the past.
targetAnswers: The stolen artwork is reported to have been found in a warehouse.
writing.explanation: When the reported past action precedes the reporting time, use the perfect passive infinitive 'to have been V3'.

writing.instruction: Complete the journalistic sentence with the correct reporting verb form: 'It is _______ that the ambassador will resign by Friday.' (allege)
writing.promptText: It is [allege] that the ambassador will resign by Friday.
writing.hint: Use the past participle form of allege.
targetAnswers: alleged
writing.explanation: The impersonal passive requires the past participle 'alleged' after 'It is'.

writing.instruction: Correct the grammar and word order error in this sentence: 'He had installed his air conditioner by a technician.'
writing.promptText: Fix the error: He had installed his air conditioner by a technician.
writing.hint: The object must come right after 'had', not the past participle.
targetAnswers: He had his air conditioner installed by a technician.
writing.explanation: In causative structures, the object ('his air conditioner') must sit directly between 'had' and the past participle ('installed').

writing.instruction: Transform into a passive reporting structure with subject: 'Journalists claim that the CEO earned millions in bonuses.'
writing.promptText: Rewrite starting with 'The CEO is claimed...':
writing.hint: Use the perfect infinitive 'to have earned'.
targetAnswers: The CEO is claimed to have earned millions in bonuses.
writing.explanation: Subject + is claimed + to have earned connects the subject to the past event correctly.

writing.instruction: Write a complete sentence using 'It is rumored that' regarding a company merger.
writing.promptText: Write a sentence using 'It is rumored that':
writing.hint: Include 'It is rumored that' followed by a complete clause about a merger.
targetAnswers: It is rumored that the two tech giants will merge next year.
It is rumored that the companies are merging.
It is rumored that a major merger is taking place.
writing.explanation: The prompt requires an impersonal passive sentence starting with 'It is rumored that' followed by a valid clause.

writing.instruction: Complete the passive reporting sentence: 'The suspect is understood _______ left the country.' (Insert missing word)
writing.promptText: The suspect is understood [missing word] left the country.
writing.hint: You need a particle before the perfect infinitive verb.
targetAnswers: to have
writing.explanation: The structure requires 'to have' before the past participle 'left' to indicate prior action.

writing.instruction: Correct the error in this passive reporting sentence: 'It was reported that the building was destroy in the fire.'

writing.hint: Check the form of the verb after 'was' in the passive clause.
targetAnswers: It was reported that the building was destroyed in the fire.
writing.explanation: Passive voice in the subordinate clause requires the past participle 'destroyed', not the base verb 'destroy'.
